raw_response:
I am 65 years old and have farmed this land in Quzhou for half a century. My father taught me, and I know every corner of my 4.1 mu. I live alone now, so I cannot afford to take risks or waste labor on things that do not pay. The wheat is already in the ground—I sowed it last October after rotary tilling the field. It is coming up green, and now, at the start of spring, I need to manage it carefully.

For my winter wheat, I will apply top-dressing urea at green-up and again at jointing, because one feeding is not enough on this soil. I have a well, so I will irrigate three times: once when I top-dress in spring, once at jointing, and once at grain filling if the weather turns dry. I will spray herbicide once and insecticide twice—there are aphids and the odd rust problem in this county. I expect about 480 kg per mu if the weather holds; that is what I usually get. I use improved wheat seed, not the old traditional grain, because the county station promoted Jimai types years ago and they do better.

After I harvest the wheat in early June, I will plant maize the same day or the next. Everyone here does summer maize after wheat, and I have no time to plough again. I will use no-tillage direct seeding with a hybrid variety—Denghai or something similar the dealer recommends. I will put down compound fertilizer at sowing and side-dress urea when the maize is knee-high. I will irrigate twice: once if the June sowing is dry, and once at the big-flare stage. Two sprays should handle weeds and the corn borer. If all goes well, I will get around 580 kg per mu of maize.

I keep my inputs moderate. I am alone and my land is small, so I do not chase the highest possible yield with extra fertilizer. I aim for steady, reliable harvests that I can manage with my own two hands and the hired machine for harvest.
